## Question and population

Within the original selected TriNetX-derived encounter population, how does documented index-encounter hypercapnia probability vary across BMI? How does availability of usable physiological evidence vary, and which original BMI ranges contribute to modeled occurrence and a specified secondary BMI contrast?

The original selected population is a selected acute-care cohort, not all acute-care patients or a national population. Select the first qualifying adult 2022 emergency/inpatient encounter with BMI ≥30 before gas availability and adjustment completeness. Earlier unresolved eligibility and earliest-date ties remain unresolved. Age uses the approved birth-year proxy. BMI comes from encounter/prior reported values or observed height and weight under the approved hierarchy; there is no statistical BMI imputation.

## Relationship and observation

Models use a natural cubic BMI spline with four fixed knots at common-reference BMI percentiles 5, 35, 65 and 95, plus linear age, sex, race/ethnicity and geographic region. Knots and factor references are fixed before outcome-specific fitting. Arterial hypercapnia uses valid unadjusted PCO2 ≥45 mm Hg. The combined definition accepts arterial ≥45 or venous ≥50; a negative means available usable specimens are below threshold. Missing or unusable gases remain unknown.

Gas curves average each fitted outcome-observed model over the common covariate-complete reference, C. ICD curves use known-capture patients, C_icd; the composite includes J96.02, J96.12, J96.22, J96.92 and E66.2. Unknown diagnosis capture is not coded negative. The ICD curve therefore describes recorded diagnoses, including obesity-containing ascertainment.

Observation curves describe usable evidence, not necessarily the decision to order testing. Probability bands are pointwise 95% full-covariance delta intervals conditional on the empirical reference. Extending gas relationships to untested patients requires an observation-exchangeability assumption. Bands do not incorporate source selection, missingness assumptions or model misspecification.

```{r}
#| label: primary-relationship
#| results: asis
figure("F1-A");caption("F1-A")
bmi_report_table(a$fixed_bmi_contrasts[a$fixed_bmi_contrasts$model_id %in% paste(c("abg","any_gas","icd"),"encounter/spline",sep="/"),],"Supported fixed-BMI 45 versus 40 contrasts; probability difference and prevalence ratio",keys="model_id")
```

## Secondary scenario and original-BMI contributions

The default scenario reduces observed BMI >30 by exactly one unit, without a floor; BMI =30 remains unchanged. It retains each patient's original index, covariates, observation status and reference membership. The model-standardized potential impact fraction is 1 − shifted probability / observed-BMI probability. It depends on the reference BMI/covariate distribution and is not a constant effect per BMI unit.

Band contributions come from paired patient predictions in original BMI bands. They sum exactly to the overall probability difference; their full covariance reproduces total uncertainty. A fixed-BMI curve multiplied by marginal BMI density is not used to calculate adjusted PIF.

```{r}
#| label: scenario-decomposition
#| results: asis
figure("F2");caption("F2")
r<-a$policy_totals
if(nrow(r)){
 ids<-paste(c("abg","any_gas","icd"),"encounter/spline",sep="/")
 primary<-r$model_id %in% ids & ((r$method=="mar" & r$reference_id=="C") | (r$method=="observed" & r$reference_id=="C_icd"))
 columns<-c("model_id","n_reference","n_model","pct_shifted","p_observed","p_shifted","difference_per1000","difference_low_per1000","difference_high_per1000","PIF","PIF_low","PIF_high")
 bmi_report_table(r[primary,columns],"Primary-reference secondary scenario; complete sensitivities are in the audit",keys="model_id")
}
```

## Supporting analyses and limitations

Calendar-day sensitivities retain the original index and require collection date equal to encounter-start date. Matched ICD/ABG and ICD/combined comparisons use identical patients within each pair. The BMI ≥40 reference reuses the broader model. Linear-BMI comparisons use identical training samples; they do not select the primary form.

The separate fixed-observation-stratum MNAR projection varies missing-outcome odds at BMI 40 and the gradient per five BMI units. Its offset is evaluated at shifted BMI too. The MAR anchor is a numerical identity, not independent confirmation. Sensitivity ranges are assumptions rather than estimated bounds. Covariates are not imputed and no observation weighting is applied.

This analysis concerns documented index-encounter occurrence. It does not estimate incidence, cases prevented or effects of within-person weight loss. Full stage profiles, every model coefficient/covariance, diagnostics, failures, sensitivity quantities and source limitations appear in the accompanying audit report and protected aggregate exports.
